channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Second person charged in connection with shooting of police officer in Nottingham
item.description: A second person has been charged in connection with the shooting of a police officer in Nottingham city centre on 18 October.

item.title: Two men killed by falling trees - as Storm Boelo recovery under way
item.description: Two men have been killed by falling trees as Storm Boelo pummelled the UK, with winds of up to 84mph, flooded streets and power cut to 800,000 homes.

item.title: What challenges await Brazil's Lula in his fourth term as president?
item.description: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will have to wrestle with a divided Brazil, an unfriendly Congress, feeble public finances and a Donald Trump-shaped menace during his unprecedented fourth term.

item.title: Trump critic Lula wins reelection in Brazil, securing fourth presidential term
item.description: Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, has been reelected in a result that provides relief to critics of Trump and keeps some distance between Latin America’s biggest economy and Washington

item.title: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
item.description: Brazil's 80-year-old left-wing leader President Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in a bitterly contested runoff.

item.title: Brazil's Lula beats odds and seals re-election, rival Bolsonaro demands annulment
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, nearly 81 years old, clinched a fourth term in a tight runoff against Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday. The leftist leader won 51.7% of the vote, compared to 48.2% for the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, official results showed. Bolsonaro has refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote.

item.title: Mariupol veteran who flew in classified mission on what every Ukrainian should know
item.description: "Everyone in Ukraine should know how to apply a tourniquet and how to stop someone's bleeding," Anatolii says.

item.title: Appeals court hears arguments in Trump admin's voting suit against California
item.description: A federal appeals court had a rare Sunday hearing in the Justice Department's voting lawsuit against California.

item.title: Report: IDF chief pushes back on Netanyahu's order
item.description: An extraordinary confrontation at the top of Israel's leadership, just two days before the election. Israeli media report Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and military chief Eyal Zamir are at odds over Iran. Zamir reportedly fears government instructions could trigger an immediate military escalation and has demanded written authorisation. Netanyahu denies any confrontation. The reports come as he warns Iran could attack Israel to disrupt Tuesday's vote.

item.title: Lula re-elected president in Brazil but his opponent refuses to accept result
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has been re-elected president of Brazil, the electoral authority has said, in a result that defied poll predictions - but his opponent has refused to accept the result.

item.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat in historic snap election with record turnout
item.description: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in an historic election on Sunday following a near to 70% turnout at polling stations – the highest since the break-up of Yugoslavia in 1992. The snap election followed nearly two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the ‌city of Novi Sad in 2024.

item.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
item.description: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

item.title: Marine Le Pen launches presidential campaign in Orléans
item.description: RN candidate Marine Le Pen officially launched her campaign for the French presidential election on Sunday, October 25, at a rally in Orléans.

item.title: Le Pen’s ‘Renaissance’: 4th time lucky?
item.description: Just before half past four, Marine Le Pen took to the stage under the stadium strobe lights at the Zénith Arena in Orléans. The radical-right leader, whom analysts say is on the doorstep of the presidency, is polarising, yet deeply and increasingly popular with her base, and has topped the popularity polls for months in France. This came 24 hours after the latest protests across the country, which included over ten thousand anti-Le Pen demonstrators outside the venue yesterday.

item.title: Lula's Legacy, Flavio's Future?
item.description: A coin-flip election in Brazil, with little separating the country's left-wing President, Lula, and his right-wing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro. The results of the run-off vote will become clear in a few hours.

item.title: US Marine indicted in alleged Okinawa robbery homicide
item.description: A 20-year-old U.S. Marine stationed in Okinawa, Japan, has been indicted on charges murder and robbery.

item.title: Talks between Ukraine, Russia and US to be held next month
item.description: A meeting between Ukraine, Russia and the US will take place next month, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

item.title: France: Football fans take over Paris as NFL comes to country for the first time
item.description: Paris's iconic Stade de France made history on Sunday, October 25, by hosting the first #NFL regular season game to ever be held in France. For this unprecedented match between the Saints and the Steelers fans flocked from New Orleans and Pittsburgh, as well as from France and other European countries. France 24's Taise Parente and Stéphanie Trouillard report.

item.title: Open Senate seat up for grabs in Iowa as candidates tout populism, bipartisanship
item.description: The once-reliably red state has become competitive turf for Democrats – and the GOP has taken notice.

item.title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.

item.title: France: Le Pen seeks to leverage unrest in presidential campaign kick-off
item.description: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally, addressed some 10,000 supporters on Sunday in the city of Orleans as she kicked off her presidential campaign, a day after nationwide cost-of-living protests flared again into violence. Le Pen, the frontrunner, is seen to be benefiting in the polls from the weeks of unrest. Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London, Andrew Smith, shares further analysis.

item.title: Opposition leader Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months in exile
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado announced on Sunday that she has returned to her homeland following almost a year in exile, after covertly leaving Venezuela in late 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. She returns as doubts about her country’s democratic future and the role of the US are growing.

item.title: Exiled opposition leader announces shock return to Venezuela
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado has returned ‌to the country nearly a year after her daring escape.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom aims for deep-red Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: In a climate where polls show Trump's approval cratering, Dems are optimistic about Scott Colom's chances of flipping Republican senator's seat in deep-red Mississippi.

item.title: French far-right leader Le Pen kicks off presidential campaign
item.description: We’ve just been listening to Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right National Rally and its presidential candidate, delivering her first official campaign speech in Orléans. She spoke of what she called a “renaissance” for France and the dawn of a new era. She also condemned what she described as “Islamist ideologies” that promote violence, saying they are incompatible with France. Our reporter Antonia Kerrigan was listening in Orléans and joins us now with more.

item.title: France: 1.314 arrested during protests across the country
item.description: France saw another day of nationwide protests on Saturday, with more than 400,000 people taking to the streets over the rising cost of living and school funding. Most marches remained peaceful, a week after riots and looting hit several cities. However, police say more than 1,300 people were arrested nationwide as violence broke out on the sidelines of demonstrations. Caroline Baum has more.

item.title: Midterms: Obama campaigns for Democrats, slams Trump
item.description: At a rally in Ohio this Saturday, former US president Barack Obama said that Americans were facing higher costs because of decisions made by the administration, including what he described as "an unnecessary war that nobody asked for and nobody voted for."

item.title: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
item.description: Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing "I am here. With you."

item.title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
item.description: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.

item.title: What makes a good spine-tingler? Stephen Graham Jones says it's all in the ending
item.description: Horror writer Stephen Graham Jones says horror's current moment is powered by more than just fear.

item.title: French far-right leader Le Pen seeks to leverage unrest in presidential campaign kick-off
item.description: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally, addressed some 10,000 supporters on Sunday in the city of Orleans as she kicked off her presidential campaign, a day after nationwide cost-of-living protests flared again into violence. Le Pen, the frontrunner, is seen to be benefiting in the polls from the weeks of unrest.

item.title: France: 110.000 protesters in Paris
item.description: Hundreds of demonstrations took place across France on Saturday over the rising cost of living, with security forces deployed in large numbers to prevent a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. While the marches themselves “passed off well” in several cities, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said members of “ultra-left” groups threw projectiles and fireworks at police in an attempt to provoke clashes. French Communist Party spokesperson Fatima Khallouk shares more details.

item.title: Calais, 10 years after the Jungle: Migrants still risk the Channel crossing
item.description: Ten years ago, in 2016, thousands of #migrants lived in what was known as the “Great #Jungle”, a vast camp on the outskirts of #Calais. It took the authorities seven days to dismantle it. Today, dozens of smaller “jungles” are scattered across a wider stretch of the coastline. These camps are dismantled every 48 hours on average. For migrants, the goal remains the same: to cross the Channel and reach the United Kingdom. Despite the risks posed by “small boats”, these makeshift vessels, many continue to attempt the crossing in the hope of a better life. Our reporters Pauline Godart, Claire Paccalin and Mohamed Farhat travelled to northern France for #BilletRetour.

item.title: Presidential runoff under way in Brazil
item.description: Brazil is also heading to the polls today for a run-off vote that will decide who leads the country. The race is on a knife edge between incumbent left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio scored a major upset in the first round earlier this month, taking the lead in the vote. The campaign has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic difficulties and allegations of US interference, which Washington has denied. France 24 correspondent Jan Onoszko reports the latest from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Le Pen leads polls with up to 38% six months before election
item.description: The day after the first day of the National Rally congress in Orléans, in central France, passed without any major incidents, Marine Le Pen is due to deliver her first major campaign speech on Sunday afternoon, 25 October, under heavy police surveillance. The speech, centred on the theme of renewal, aims to inject a dose of optimism six months ahead of the presidential election, the candidate has reportedly said in private. Gilles Ivaldi, a political science researcher at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the University of Nice, explains that the violence following protests across France in recent weeks could help the National Rally present itself as the party capable of restoring public safety and national security.

item.title: France: Le Pen launches presidential campaign in Orleans
item.description: Far-right leader Marine Le Pen is launching her presidential campaign today. The National Rally candidate is due to deliver her first campaign speech in Orléans, addressing around 10,000 party members. Police were controlling traffic entering the city this morning, following a large anti-far-right demonstration on Saturday, where thousands of protesters marched chanting anti-fascist slogans.

item.title: The week in pictures: Protests across France, wildfires in Indonesia and Brazilian elections
item.description: From student protests across France over the weekend and presidential elections in Brazil pitting leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro to wildfires in Indonesia, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: Lula thanks voters for his victory, Flavio Bolsonaro does not recognize the results
item.description: It is the first time in the country’s history since the return of democracy that a candidate who lost in the first round manages to come back and win in the runoff. The left-wing president obtained 51.7% of the votes, compared with the 48.2% received by right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Polls open in Brazil presidential runoff
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and sight-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro faced off Friday in their second and final debate ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff election. The two candidates repeated their campaign proposals, focusing on the cost of living and security, while exchanging ⁠allegations of corruption. France 24 Jan Onoszko telles us the latest from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
item.description: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

item.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
item.description: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.

item.title: Bus and lorry collide killing 22, including passengers returning from funeral
item.description: At least 22 people have been killed after a bus and lorry collided in Kenya, police say.

item.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
item.description: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

item.title: Independent candidates sense a moment. Some Democrats hope they're right.
item.description: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.

item.title: Serbia's pro-Russian leader urges supporters to avoid 'killings' after defeat
item.description: Serbia's long-serving pro-Russian leader has urged his supporters to avoid "killings" after he conceded defeat to a student-led movement at the election.

item.title: Brazilians head to the polls with left-winger and son of Trump ally neck and neck
item.description: Brazilians are going to the polls today to elect a president in a run-off vote that is being closely watched around the world.

item.title: Early voting begins in New York: What to know and the key races to watch
item.description: Saturday is the first day of early voting in New York and Empire State voters could help decide which party will control the House over the next two years.

item.description: A power surge at Stansted Airport has caused hundreds of flights to be delayed.
